messages.content: help me write a short letter to my neighbor. she gave me a book to read, and i have finished it. i want to thank her and ask when i can bring it back.
thank you for the book. i have finished reading it and would like to bring it back. when would be a good time for you?
i liked the story, but i do not want to say it was the best book in the world.
you can add a simple sentence: i enjoyed the story. that says what you liked without saying it was better than every other book.
show me the letter with that sentence added.
thank you for the book. i enjoyed the story and have finished reading it. when would be a good time to bring it back?
now make the last part a choice between this evening and tomorrow morning.
would this evening or tomorrow morning be a good time to bring it back?
put it all together, but leave out that i finished it. asking to bring it back is enough.
thank you for the book. i enjoyed the story. would this evening or tomorrow morning be a good time to bring it back?
if she says tomorrow morning, should i still bring it this evening?
no. she has chosen tomorrow morning. if that no longer works for you, ask about another time before going.
write a reply saying tomorrow morning works for me.
tomorrow morning works for me. thank you again for the book.
should you add that i will come at nine?
only if that is the hour you want to give. so far you have chosen the morning, not a specific hour.
tell me a story about a teacher, a student, and a picture. the teacher should give the picture to the student, and the student should show it to her mother at home.

a teacher found an old picture of the town. she showed it to a group at school and asked which places they could still see in the town today. one student saw the library and the tree near its door. the teacher gave her the picture to take home for the evening. after dinner, the student showed it to her mother. her mother remembered the old library door and told her about visiting it as a child. the student put the picture in her book so she could bring it back to school the next day.
who had the picture first in the story?
the teacher had it first.
who remembered visiting the old library as a child?
the mother.
did the student give the picture to her mother to keep?
no. she showed it to her mother, then put it in her own book to bring back to school.
make a question whose answer is after dinner.
when did the student show the picture to her mother?
now answer that question with a full sentence.
she showed the picture to her mother after dinner.
if the student says my mother remembered the door, who is my about?
my is about the student who says the sentence. she is talking about her own mother.
can you change that sentence to the voice of someone telling the story about the student?
her mother remembered the door.
what did the teacher ask the group to find?
places in the old picture that they could still see in the town today.
i like learning alone, but my friend asked if we could read together. i do not want to say yes to a whole afternoon before trying it.
you could choose a short time first. that would let you try reading together without giving the whole afternoon to it.
what could i say without making it sound as if i think she will make it hard?
would you like to read together for a little while first? i usually study alone, so i would like to see how it works for me.
she asked whether we should read the same page or different books. which is right?
either can work. do you want to talk about one page together or simply have someone near while you read?
i want to talk about one page because we both found it hard.
then reading the same page can help with your goal. you can each say what you think it is about and look again at the parts that are not clear.
we do not want you to give us an answer before we try.
then i can wait while you try. when you are ready, you can ask about a specific sentence or give me your idea to check.
what is one question we could ask each other first?
what do you think this page is about?
can you make that question shorter?
what is this page about?
now make it a question about one sentence rather than the whole page.
what is this sentence about?
can that be useful even if we give different answers at first?
yes. the difference can help you see what each of you understood and which parts you need to read again.
the library is open this afternoon, so my brother says i can go. but i have to work. how can i explain the difference?
the library being open can mean people can visit it. it does not give you free time when you have to work.
say that in two short sentences.
the library is open for people to visit. you are still busy with work.
write a short reply to him.
the library is open, but i am not free this afternoon. i have to work.
now he says i should go tomorrow instead. i do not know my work plan for tomorrow yet.
then you can say tomorrow might work, but you need to check your work plan first.
can you say that without making it sound like i have already chosen tomorrow?
tomorrow may work. i need to check my work plan before choosing a time.
what if i check and find i am free in the morning?
then you know when you are free. you would still need to know whether the library is open tomorrow morning.
so two things have to work together?
yes. you need time when you are free and the library is open.
give that idea in one short sentence.
i can go when i am free and the library is open.
does today being open tell you tomorrow is open too?
not for sure. the information you gave was about this afternoon.
write two examples, one with i have and one with she has. use a book in each.
i have a book. she has a book.
now make them questions with do and does.
do i have a book? does she have a book?
why did has become have in the question?
after does in that question, use have. the sentence without does is she has a book.
what if i want to ask her myself?
you can ask: do you have a book?
now she answers that she does. give a short answer in her voice.
yes, i do.
can she also say yes, i have a book?
yes. that is a full answer with the same basic meaning.
what if she wants to say the book is in her room?
she can say: yes, i have a book in my room.
write it as a sentence about her, not her own words.
she has a book in her room.
if i keep my room instead, what changes?
then you could be saying the book is in your room rather than hers.
give only the sentence that keeps it in her room.
she has a book in her room.
i was going to make dinner for myself, but a friend called and asked to come over. i have rice, vegetables, and eggs. help me think without giving a long cooking plan.
you could first ask whether your friend wants to eat with you. if so, check whether the food you have is enough for both of you.
she does want dinner, and i have enough. she does not eat eggs.
then leave the eggs out of the food you make for her. rice and vegetables may work, but you can ask whether she likes that choice.
she says rice and vegetables sound good. do i need to make another meal just for myself?
not unless you want one. you can both have rice and vegetables if that works for you too.
i want eggs as well, but i do not want them in her food.
then you can keep the eggs apart and add them only to your own plate.
write a message telling her what the plan is.
i can make rice and vegetables for us. i will keep the eggs apart and only add them to my own plate.
why is us right there rather than her?
because you are writing to your friend about food for both of you. us can mean you and the person you are talking to.
give me just the meaning of us here.
us can mean you and your friend together in this message.
now make the message shorter.
we can have rice and vegetables. i will keep the eggs on my own plate.
did i say she does not like eggs?
no. you said she does not eat them. you did not give a reason.
write a short story that stops before a girl opens a letter. i want to choose what is inside later.

a girl came home from school and found a letter on the table. her father said it had come that morning. she turned it over and saw her name written clearly on the front. she carried it to the chair by the window, where the light was good. for a moment she just held it and thought about who might have sent it. then she put her book down, sat in the chair, and got ready to open the letter.
give me just the sentence about what she thought, without saying who sent it.
for a moment she just held it and thought about who might have sent it.
now could i choose that it was from her aunt?
yes. the story has not said who sent it, so you can choose her aunt for the next part.
write two more sentences where she opens it and sees a picture from her aunt. do not make it a photo of a place i have not chosen.
she opened the letter and found a picture inside. a short message from her aunt was written on the back.
what did you leave for me to choose?
you can still choose what the picture is of and what her aunt wrote.
can you now say the picture is of the garden without changing the first part?
yes. the first part does not say what the picture is of, so a garden can work.
write the next sentence with the garden alone in the picture.
the picture was of a garden with a small tree near the middle.
now make the tree near the front rather than the middle.
the picture was of a garden with a small tree near the front.
my neighbor let me use a tool for one day. i gave it back this morning. can i say i gave my neighbor a tool?
you can, but that leaves out something important: you were giving the tool back. i returned the tool is more clear about that.
make a full sentence with returned.
i returned the tool to my neighbor this morning.
now use the tool i used instead, and leave my neighbor out.
i returned the tool i used this morning.
could that mean i used it this morning rather than returned it this morning?
yes. the words this morning could seem to go with used. you can put the time first to make the return clear.
show me.
this morning, i returned the tool i had used.
does had used show the use was before the return?
yes. it puts the use before the return in that sentence.
now write a short thank you to my neighbor.
thank you for the help. i have brought the tool back.
can you add that it was useful?
thank you for the help. the tool was useful, and i have brought it back.
can i say it is mine now because i used it?
no. using it for a day did not make it yours. you said your neighbor let you use it and you returned it.
is she do her work right? give the correct sentence first, then one sentence of explanation.
she does her work. use does with she in this sentence.
now make it a question, again with the answer first.
does she do her work? use do after does in this question.
if i say yes, she does, do i have to say her work again?
no. if the question is already clear, yes, she does can be enough.
make a longer yes answer that has her work in it.
yes, she does her work.
now make a no answer.
no, she does not do her work.
what if the question is only about today?
then you can make that clear in a new question: does she have work to do today? no, she does not have work to do today.
now ask whether she is doing her work right now, and give a full no answer.
is she doing her work now? no, she is not doing her work now.
if i just want the short no answer to that new question?
no, she is not.
why not no, she does not this time?
because the new question starts with is she, so the short answer is she is not.
give me the question and short answer only.
is she doing her work now? no, she is not.
there is a song i remember from when i was a child, but i do not know its name. i only remember hearing my grandmother sing it in her kitchen.
that sounds like a memory with a person and a place, even without the song name. do you remember any of the words?
no, just the sound of her voice. i am not asking you to find it yet.
then we can talk about the memory itself. what do you remember about being in the kitchen with her?
she would cook, and i would sit at the table drawing. sometimes she asked me to sing with her.
so the song was part of time you spent together. she cooked while you drew, and sometimes you would sing with her.
can you turn that into a few sentences in my voice?

when i was a child, i sat at the kitchen table drawing while my grandmother cooked. sometimes she would sing and ask me to sing with her. i do not remember the name of the song, but i remember the sound of her voice.
now leave out the drawing.

when i was a child, i spent time in the kitchen while my grandmother cooked. sometimes she would sing and ask me to sing with her. i do not remember the name of the song, but i remember the sound of her voice.
did i tell you she would sing every day?
no. you said sometimes, not every day.
keep that difference if i ask for the story again.
yes. sometimes keeps the meaning you gave, while every day would add a detail you did not give.
help me use between and after. the chair is in the space with the table on one side and the window on the other.
you can say: the chair is between the table and the window.
what if i walk past the table and then reach the chair?
you can say: i went past the table and then got to the chair.
could you use after that to join those parts?
i went past the table. after that, i got to the chair.
is that the same as the chair being between the table and window?
not always. the first sentence gives the place of the chair. the other gives the order of what you did while walking.
give that answer in fewer words.
not always. one sentence gives the place of the chair. the other gives the order of what you did.
could both sentences be true?
yes. the chair can be between the table and the window, and you can go past the table before getting to it.
now put a book on the chair. where is the book?
on the chair, which is between the table and the window.
does that mean the book is on the table too?
no. you put it on the chair. being near the table is different from being on it.
give me a very short but clear place answer.
the book is on the chair.
i asked my brother to bring a book. he brought one, but it was not the one i wanted. did my first request tell him which one?
not from those words alone. a book leaves the choice open unless the conversation already makes a specific book clear.
we had not talked about a book before. i wanted the one with a picture of a tree on the front.
then that detail would help him choose. you can ask for the book with the tree picture on the front.
what if there are two books with a tree picture?
then you need another detail that keeps them apart, such as where the book is or what color it is.
one is green and one is blue. i want the blue one.
you can say: please bring the blue book with a tree picture on the front.
is all that detail always needed?
no. you only need enough to make the choice clear. if the blue book is already clear between you, please bring the blue book may be enough.
now he is holding both and asks this one as he holds up the blue one. what can i say?
yes, that one.
why can such a short answer work now?
because he has held up a specific book. that one can mean the book you can both see.
say it another way.
you can both see which book he is asking about, so that one can be clear without saying the whole request again.
my friend sent me okay. does that mean she is not happy with me?
not for sure. okay is short, but a short reply alone does not tell you how she feels.
we were choosing a time for lunch. i said one, and she said okay.
in that context, it can simply be an answer saying one works for her. you have not given a clear reason to think she is not happy with you.
what if i want to check the lunch plan instead of asking about her feelings?
you can ask: are we still meeting for lunch at one?
would that be too much if she already said okay?
if the plan is clear to both of you, you may not need another question. if you are not sure, a short check can help.
i think i just read a feeling into a small word.
that can happen with short messages because you cannot hear the voice. it may help to keep the reply in the context of the question she was answering.
write a simple sentence i can remember about that.
a short message does not always give a clear feeling.
now she sends see you at one. what do i know?
she has said she will see you at one. that makes the lunch plan more clear.
can i know she will be happy the whole day?
no. a message about meeting for lunch does not tell us how she will feel for the whole day.
write a story using before, after, and while. use a boy making a picture while his father reads.

before dinner, a boy put paper on the kitchen table and began drawing a picture. while he drew, his father sat near the window reading. after finishing the picture, the boy carried it over to show his father. his father put the book down and looked at the drawing. then they put the paper on a shelf and went to get dinner ready together.
did dinner happen before the drawing?
no. the drawing began before dinner.
was the father reading while the boy was drawing?
yes. those things happened at the same time in the story.
what happened after the picture was finished?
the boy carried it to his father and showed it to him.
can you give the story in three sentences?
before dinner, a boy drew a picture while his father read by the window. after finishing it, he showed it to his father. they put the picture on a shelf and got dinner ready together.
does the short story still say every detail from the first one?
no. it keeps the order and the important things they did, but leaves out some details, such as where the paper was at first.
where was it at first?
on the kitchen table.
now give just a sentence with while about both people.
while the boy was drawing, his father was reading by the window.
i tried to draw a tree and did not like the picture. i think i cannot draw anything.
one picture you do not like does not tell you what every picture will be like. what part of the tree was hard for you?
the whole shape. i kept making it too large for the page.
then the size on the page is a specific thing you can work on. you could try a smaller shape before adding details.
i do not want another whole picture right now.
that is okay. you can leave it for now. one hard try does not mean you have to keep working until you are happy with it.
can you say something kind without telling me it must be a good drawing?
you tried something hard, and you can take a rest without calling the whole try wrong.
my friend liked the color. i did like that part too.
then you found one part you both liked, even though the shape did not work how you wanted.
help me say both things in one sentence.
i like the color, but i want to make the tree smaller next time.
does that say i hate the whole picture?
no. it says what you liked and what you want to change.
what if next time is not today?
then you can still keep that idea for another day. next time does not have to mean today.
i am at home, and my sister is at school. i want her to have her book. should i say i will bring it to you or i will take it to you?
both can be clear in a message to her. bring it to you can mean you are coming to her with it. take it to school can mean you are moving it from home to school.
give me just the difference in two short sentences.
bring it to you can mean you are coming to her with it. take it to school can mean you are moving it from home to school.
what could she ask me from school?
can you bring my book to school?
now what could i tell my father at home before i leave?
i am taking the book to school for my sister.
does taking mean the book is mine?
no. it says what you are doing with the book, not whose book it is.
if my sister later talks to her teacher about what i did, what could she say without saying whether i am a boy or girl?
someone from my family brought my book to school.
could she use my name instead if she knows it?
yes. she could use your name to make clear which person brought the book.
make it about my sister bringing the book to me instead.
my sister brought my book to school.
is that now a new example rather than the same first story?
yes. you changed who brought the book and who got it.
my friend and i chose the library for our visit. now i want the park because it is warm outside. can i just tell her we are meeting at the park?
you can ask whether she would like to change the place. because you chose the library together, it is useful to check before making the park the new plan.
write just the question.
it is warm outside. would you like to meet at the park instead of the library?
she says she needs to return a book first.
then the library still has a reason to be part of the plan. you could ask whether she wants to go to the park after returning the book.
write that without choosing for her.
would you like to go to the park after you return your book?
she says yes, if there is time. have we chosen to stay in the park all afternoon?
no. she said yes only if there is time. you have not chosen how long to stay in the park.
what is the plan we share?
you will meet at the library, and you may go to the park after she gives her book back if there is time.
say it more simply.
first you will meet at the library. after she gives the book back, you may go to the park if there is time.
now say it as my message to her.
let us meet at the library first. we can go to the park after you give the book back if there is time.
write four short sentences about a room. there is a table near the window, a chair under the clock, and a book on the table. do not add people.
the table is near the window. the chair is under the clock. the book is on the table. the book and chair are in the same room.
if i say do not add people, does that mean you should write no people are in the room?
no. i should write about the objects you gave without saying the room is empty. leaving people out of the writing does not tell us whether anyone is there.
give the four sentences again without adding anything about people.
the table is near the window. the chair is under the clock. the book is on the table. the book and chair are in the same room.
is the last sentence something you can get from what i gave?
yes. you said these objects were in a room, so saying they are in the same room keeps that information.
now make the writing two sentences instead.
a table with a book on it stands near the window. a chair is under the clock.
can you tell me the color of the book?
not from the information you gave.
i add that it is blue. show me the two sentences again.
a table with a blue book on it stands near the window. a chair is under the clock.
keep the chair under the clock, not under the table.
yes. the chair is under the clock in those sentences.
can you join these ideas with although: i was tired. i finished the page.
although i was tired, i finished the page.
does that say i was not really tired?
no. it keeps both ideas true: you were tired, and you still finished the page.
keep both ideas and use but.
you were tired, but you still finished the page.
can although come in the middle instead?
yes. i finished the page although i was tired.
what if i say because i was tired instead of although i was tired?
because gives a reason for what happened. although keeps both facts together without making being tired the reason you finished.
give me one sentence with because and one with although, using a walk.
although it was cold, we went for a walk. because it was cold, we stayed inside.
can you say the difference with what happened in each example?
in the first example, we walked even though it was cold. in the other, the cold was why we stayed inside.
are those examples about the same walk?
not always. they are two grammar examples with different choices. they do not have to be about one real day.
give me the short answer.
they are two different examples. one has a walk, and the other has people inside.
i enjoyed talking about my garden today. i need to go now, but maybe i will tell you about the new flowers another day.
it was good to hear about your garden. you can tell me about the flowers when you want to.
do not ask me to come back at a specific time.
okay. there is no need to choose a time now.
can you give me a short goodbye with something about the garden?
goodbye. i hope you enjoy some quiet time in the garden.
what if i am going to work, not to the garden?
then i should not say the garden is where you are going next. i can simply say: goodbye. i hope your day goes well.
make it one sentence.
goodbye, and i hope your day goes well.
will you know what flowers i mean if i come back in a new conversation?
not from this conversation alone if the new conversation does not have it. you may need to tell me again which flowers you mean.
then do not say you will remember everything.
i should only use the context i have. you can give the garden details again if they are needed later.
thanks. just goodbye now.
goodbye.
